guided_practice.title: Plan coverage
guided_practice.prompt: Name five distinct categories for the chooser evaluation.
guided_practice.answer: Ordinary selection, duration boundaries, invalid records, empty/no-match input and ties/order reversal.

independent_case.title: Evaluate independently
independent_case.task: Given ordinary 3/3, boundary 1/2, invalid 2/2 and tie 0/1, compute overall results and prioritize issues.
independent_case.answer: 6/8 pass, 2 fail; boundary has one failure and ties fail the only case. Report both and avoid treating 75 percent as production accuracy.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: A successful run proves the conclusion

For a rule-based chooser, evaluate conformance to its policy separately from whether users find suggestions useful. Neither a pass fraction nor an invented satisfaction score proves educational benefit.

Require the new W4 case, explicit predictions and an explanation. Fresh retry: ordinary 2/2, empty 0/1, boundary 2/2 gives 4/5 overall; the empty case still fails. Require the failure record and a fresh-case plan.

Hiding the tie failure in an average conceals an unmet requirement. Preserve the failed input, expected result, actual result and version. If you repair using it, classify it as development/regression evidence and reserve new final cases.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
checks = [{"category": "ordinary", "passed": True},
          {"category": "ordinary", "passed": True},
          {"category": "boundary", "passed": True},
          {"category": "invalid", "passed": True},
          {"category": "empty", "passed": True},
          {"category": "tie", "passed": False}]
passed = 0
for check in checks:
    if check["passed"]:
        passed = passed + 1
print(passed, len(checks))

blocks.text: The script reports 5 and 6. About 83.3 percent of these checks pass, but that is not an accuracy estimate for all future use. The cases were deliberately chosen, their frequencies are artificial, and each category has few cases.

The six development checks include ordinary, boundary, invalid, empty and tie cases. Five pass, but the only tie case fails. Saying five out of six pass is true; saying the tie rule works is false. Keep both statements visible. A category table helps you choose the next repair. Adding many copies of passing ordinary cases can raise the overall fraction without checking a new condition or fixing the failed requirement.
